official.deadline_central_display: mid-September (U.S. Embassies and Fulbright Commissions must submit nominations to IIE); each country sets its own earlier internal deadline
official.deadline_note: Application deadlines vary by country and are set by the nominating U.S. Embassy or Binational Fulbright Commission, which advises applicants of its internal deadline. For the 2027-2028 round, country deadlines ran from late June to end of August 2026 (e.g. Tanzania 30 June 2026; Algeria 21 July 2026; Nigeria, Ghana, Croatia, Serbia and Oman 31 July 2026; Israel 15 August 2026; Jamaica 31 August 2026).
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 cycle (application window closed in summer 2026; next round expected to open in spring 2027)
official.status_note: The 2027-2028 competition is closed to new applications: country deadlines fell between June and August 2026 and nominations were due to IIE by mid-September 2026. Independent U.S. review follows, with final selections announced around March-April 2027 and fellows starting in the United States between August and September 2027. The next (2028-2029) round is expected to open in spring 2027; confirm dates with your nominating post.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Payment of tuition and fees at the assigned host university

A maintenance (living) allowance, including a one-time settling-in allowance
Air travel (international travel to and from the U.S. for the Program and domestic travel to required program events)
A Professional Development allowance for professional activities, such as field trips, professional visits, and conferences
eligibility: Be a citizen of an eligible country
Have an undergraduate (first university or Bachelor's) degree
Have a minimum of five years of full-time professional experience
Demonstrated leadership qualities and a record of public service in the community
Limited experience in the United States
Prior time in the United States should not have been substantial (more than three years), with at least four years since then back home employed at a level of professional responsibility

Complete answers to all questions; essay responses in English must thoroughly address the prompt
Two letters of recommendation in English; one must be from the applicant's current employer
Official transcripts in English listing courses taken and grades received; diplomas need only be uploaded if the transcript does not show proof that the degree was obtained
Demonstrated English language ability; TOEFL alternatives such as IELTS or Duolingo English Test can be utilized for all candidates
Meet any country-specific requirements published by the nominating post (which may add documents such as a passport scan or signed employer confirmation letter)
documents: Online application completed in English at apply.iie.org/huberthhumphrey, accessed through your nominating U.S. Embassy or Binational Fulbright Commission
Essay responses to the application prompts, in English
Two letters of recommendation in English, one from the applicant's current employer
Official transcripts in English listing courses taken and grades received; diploma/degree certificate only if the transcript does not prove the degree was obtained
English test score (TOEFL, or alternatives such as IELTS or Duolingo English Test) where required by the nominating post
Country-specific additions where required, e.g. passport scan, signed employer confirmation letter in English, notarized translations of non-English documents
selection_criteria: Potential for leadership and a demonstrated commitment to public service in the public or private sector
Professional experience and interest in the policy aspects of the field of study applied for
English language ability sufficient for graduate-level, non-degree study in the United States
National shortlisting and interview by the nominating U.S. Embassy or Binational Fulbright Commission
After national selection, independent review committees review nominations in the United States, and final candidate approval is determined by the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board

Candidates are reviewed and selected based on their field of study, not their geographic region; fellows are assigned in groups of 13-15 to the most appropriate host institution and cannot choose their university
coverage: Tuition and fees at the assigned host university
Monthly maintenance (living) allowance, including a one-time settling-in allowance
International air travel to and from the U.S. for the Program plus domestic travel to required program events
Professional Development allowance for professional activities, such as field trips, professional visits, and conferences
application_method: Contact the U.S. Embassy (Public Affairs Section) or Binational Fulbright Commission in your country to access the Humphrey Fellowship application and learn its internal deadline; in 28 countries the program is administered by a Binational Fulbright Commission, and in all other participating countries by the Public Affairs Section of the U.S. Embassy
Complete the online application in English at apply.iie.org/huberthhumphrey
National selection: shortlisted applicants are interviewed by the post (typically late summer), and the post then submits its nominations to the Institute of International Education by mid-September
U.S. review by independent committees and final approval by the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board; fellows are notified by their post of their status
official.application_route: Apply online at apply.iie.org/huberthhumphrey after registering through your country's U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section or Binational Fulbright Commission - direct applications to the program are not accepted.
official.study_mode: Full-time, in-person, non-degree program at a U.S. host university (the program describes itself as quite rigorous, with many required activities)
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be citizens of an eligible participating country (the program publishes a country eligibility list of approximately 148 participating countries). Nominating posts may add residency rules - for example, Oman requires applicants to reside in Oman at application and throughout the selection process, and the U.S. Embassy Jerusalem post covers Palestinian residents of Jerusalem, the West Bank or Gaza.
official.international_eligibility: Designed for international professionals: eligibility is limited to citizens of eligible participating countries, so the fellowship is not open to U.S. citizens or U.S.-based applicants.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants apply in one of the program's published fields of study, grouped under four impact areas - Human & Institutional Capacity (Economic Development; Finance and Banking; Public Policy Analysis and Public Administration; Technology Policy and Management), Rights & Freedoms (Communications/Journalism; Law and Human Rights), Sustainable Lands (Agricultural and Rural Development; Natural Resources, Sustainability, and Environmental Policy; Urban and Regional Planning), and Thriving Communities (Public Health Policy and Management; Substance Abuse Education, Treatment and Prevention; Educational Administration, Planning, and Policy). Some posts list these consolidated into six main fields.
official.duration: Ten-month fellowship year of non-degree, graduate-level study, plus an eight-week pre-academic program of intensive English language and professional training where required, and a six-week Professional Affiliation
official.description: The Humphrey Fellowship, a Fulbright exchange, advances American interests by bringing influential professionals from priority countries to the United States to build strategic partnerships that advance shared interests, through graduate-level, non-degree study and professional experiences at U.S. host universities and organizations. The program is a Fulbright exchange activity sponsored by the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government and administered by the Institute of International Education.
official.program_type: Non-degree professional fellowship for mid-career professionals (Fulbright exchange)
official.english_requirement: Demonstrated English language ability; the program states that testing alternatives such as IELTS or Duolingo English Test can be utilized for all candidates in place of TOEFL. No central minimum score is published - the nominating Embassy or Fulbright Commission advises on eligibility, and some posts require finalists to sit a TOEFL.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a nomination-only Fulbright exchange: you cannot apply straight to IIE, because your only route runs through the U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section or Binational Fulbright Commission in your own country, and their internal deadlines (roughly June to August) close well before the mid-September central nomination date. It is a ten-month, non-degree program, so you will not earn a degree, you will not choose your university, and you will be placed with a cohort matched to your professional field. The award covers tuition and fees, a location-based living allowance, insurance, books, a computer subsidy and travel, but nothing for dependents, so any family costs are entirely yours. The 2027-2028 round closed in summer 2026 with final selections due March-April 2027, so plan now for the 2028-2029 competition.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals with five or more years of post-degree, policy-facing experience in a Humphrey field who want intensive U.S. professional exposure without committing to a degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the program's eligibility list and identify your nominating U.S. Embassy or Fulbright Commission before anything else
Contact that post in the first quarter of the application year to obtain its internal deadline, which is usually the binding one
Register on apply.iie.org/huberthhumphrey early and prepare transcripts that list both courses taken and grades received, in English
Line up two referees now, one of whom must be your current employer, and brief them on the essay prompts before they are asked
Draft essays around the two questions the posts emphasise: why this programme at this exact point in your career, and what your home country gains
Prepare TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo early, since several posts require shortlisted finalists to sit a TOEFL inside a tight interview window
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to IIE, or missing your country's internal deadline, which leaves the nominating post unable to put you forward
Being a recent graduate or relying on part-time work: five years of full-time, post-degree professional experience is a hard floor
Essays that restate your CV instead of answering the prompt about career timing and home-country impact
A recommendation set that omits your current employer, or letters submitted in a language other than English
Transcripts that are unofficial, untranslated, or missing grades, plus country-specific rules on notarised translations that catch applicants late
Choosing a field of study that does not match your professional record, because review is by field rather than by region
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Costs for accompanying dependents: the programme pays no additional maintenance allowance for dependents and requires proof of financial support, State-Department-compliant insurance and childcare plans before J-2 visas are approved. Anything beyond the published book, computer and professional-development allowances falls to the Fellow.
document_audit: Transcripts must list courses taken AND grades received; a diploma is only needed where the transcript does not prove the degree was obtained

Non-English transcripts and diplomas generally need translation, and the standard differs by post - notarised translations in Croatia, certified translated copies in Burundi - so check your own post's rule
Some posts require supplementary documents mailed separately with their own earlier deadline, such as Serbia's mailed reference documents due a week before the application deadline
Several posts add a passport scan and a signed employer confirmation letter in English that your employer must produce
Shortlisted applicants should expect an in-person interview in English and, at some posts, a programme-funded TOEFL completed before the packet goes to Washington
alerts: Deadlines are national, not central: for the 2027-2028 round they ranged from 30 June to 31 August 2026 across posts, so the FAQ's 'mid-September' figure is the nomination cut-off for posts, not your application date
You cannot choose your host university; placement is by field and in cohorts of 13-15 fellows
No degree is awarded, and the programme is deliberately demanding, so plan for ten months fully away from your job
More than three years of prior experience in the United States is disqualifying unless you have since spent at least four years back home at a level of professional responsibility
The programme provides no dependent allowance, and not all countries permit fellows to bring dependents during the fellowship year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register through your nominating post, submit the English online application at apply.iie.org/huberthhumphrey by that post's deadline, then post-level shortlisting and interview; nominated packets reach IIE by mid-September for independent U.S. review and Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board approval.
